messages:
infra-bot: :warning: ALERT: host gpu-23 (us-west1) emitting repeated Xid 31/13 resets and rising ECC correctable counters. Initial spike observed ~5m ago. Some pods auto-evacuated. pinging @sara @rory oncall

sara: I can see multiple Xid 13 and Xid 31 entries in dmesg, and several inference workers OOM-killed. Traffic error rate up for a slice of customers. starting live triage.

rory: on it. which node pool and billing tier? can you paste `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `kubectl describe node` output?

sara: node is in dedicated-gpu-pool-1. ECC snippet:
```
GPU 0
    ECC Errors
        Volatile: corrected: 142, uncorrected: 0
        Aggregate: corrected: 148
```
also seeing `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00): 31, pid=4123, pidName=python` in journal. pods running batched generation got killed.

mike (eng-runtime): note that client retries are causing bursts; recommend reducing retry aggressiveness temporarily to avoid amplifying pressure on warm capacity.

rory: Plan: cordon gpu-23 and drain. try a graceful driver restart after draining. if resets persist, hardware swap.

amanda (customer-success): opening customer bridge for impacted Dedicated tenants; we have two customers with >5% errors in the last 3m. sending initial notice.

sara: beginning `kubectl drain gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`. A few pods stuck Terminating due to local checkpoints.

mike: if pods hang, force-delete after 45s and capture pod yaml + local volumes for investigation. avoid mass rollout across pool.

deploy-bot: migration report: most pods rescheduled. 4 pods pending due to GPU quota elsewhere; fallback routing engaged for those jobs.

rory: restarted driver steps: `systemctl restart nvidia-drm && modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && modprobe nvidia_uvm`. Driver came up but dmesg still logs intermittent Xid 31. ECC correctable counters still creeping.

sara: found a container crash trace referencing cuBLAS; attaching snippet:
```
[  +0.000000] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:00): 31, pid=4123, pidName=python
```

mike: temporary mitigation: reduce `max_batch_tokens` for heavy routes and enable fallback model variants with lower memory to get pending pods running.

rory: applied throttle policy to dedicated-gpu-pool-1 via runtime config; reduced batch size by 30% for known heavy endpoints.

amanda: customer bridge note sent: "We’re mitigating GPU driver resets; some requests may see errors or extra latency. We'll post updates in 30 minutes."

infra-bot: hardware partner notified for gpu-23 — requesting ECC memory scan and physical inspection; ETA TBD.

sara: health checks run:
```
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
journalctl -u nvidia-driver --since "10 minutes ago" | tail -n 200
smartctl -a /dev/sda
```
no disk SMART failures; GPU temp ~76-80C under load.

rory: thermal could be contributing. throttling noisy workloads and scheduling maintenance to reseat/replace card.

mike: enabled conservative kernel/JIT limits and toggled nv_peer_mem fallback to reduce cross-process exposure; monitoring for regressions.

amanda: CS impact summary:
- Affected: 2 Dedicated customers, several self-serve tenants on warm pool.
- Symptoms: 8-12% request errors, median latency +100-150ms for impacted routes.
- External message: "Investigating GPU driver resets; workloads being moved; updates in 30m."

sara: handing off to night oncall @rory in ~25m. Current status: node cordoned, most pods drained, driver restart did not fully stop Xid events, ECC correctable counts rising but no uncorrected errors. Hardware ticket open.

rory: runbook for next oncall:
- monitor `dmesg` for Xid regressions
- check `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` every 10m and log counters
- keep node cordoned until hardware swap or stable cool-down for >=2h
- escalate immediately on any uncorrected ECC or persistent Xid spikes
- document which customers had fallback routing enabled

amanda: prepping postmortem and will update customer bridge after hardware partner confirms swap window.

infra-bot: Incident assigned to rory (oncall). severity: page. Ticket INF-2026-4682. Next automated update in 30m or on status change.

rory: uploaded core dump and container logs to S3: `s3://redwood-incident-archive/2461234567/core-dumps/gpu-23/`. Added to ticket.

sara: action items:
- sara: attach full logs + telemetry to ticket
- rory: coordinate hardware partner swap/reseat window
- mike: validate fallback model correctness and replay failing requests against fallback
- amanda: customer comms and tracking

mike: one more config note — if Xid continues after reschedules, consider temporary capacity-shed across pool to keep Dedicated SLAs intact.

rory: night oncall escalation contact: infra oncall +1-555-0102. If Xid counters jump after reschedule/escalate immediately.

amanda: will update bridge when hardware partner confirms replacement window. Thanks team.

infra-bot: STATUS UPDATE @+30m: Node remains cordoned. ECC correctable rate slowed but not stopped. No uncorrected ECC observed. Hardware partner response: investigating thermal degradation; reseat or swap likely recommended."
